pull.title: fix(harnesses): the server writes every agent's model list, the launcher reads it
pull.body:
## The report

```
PS> mcc-opencode
My Claude Code warning: could not prepare the OpenCode config (timed out); launching without an MCC provider.
```

OpenCode started with no MCC models in the picker. On the machine that reported
it, it would have done that on every launch, forever.

## What was actually wrong

Three defects compounded into a deadlock, none of them in the generated document
(OpenCode 1.18.26 loads it and lists every MCC model with zero errors).

**Wrong budget.** `cli/harnesses/catalogue_client.py` imported
`PROXY_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.5` from `cli/launchers/common.py` and used
it as the socket timeout for `GET /admin/api/catalogue-models`. That constant is
sized for `GET /health`, which answers in milliseconds. The route it was applied
to serialises **all thirteen** registered harness documents out of the resolution
ladder and measured **1.8–4.0 s** on the reporting install (1.41 MB response,
reproduced 3/3 through the launcher's own code path). The name is where the bug
lived: nothing about `PROXY_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` says it is also the budget
for a multi-second serialisation.

**Wrong shape.** Most of that time was provenance. `capability_payload` walked
the ladder once per field per model — 2.74 ms/model warm × 292 models, so ~0.8 s
warm and ~5 s on a cold models.dev index — computed for the Models page and read
by nobody on this route. The launchers consume `document`, `model_count` and
`defaulted`; `defaulted` comes from the serialiser, not from provenance. The
whole walk was bought and thrown away on every launch.

**Wrong recovery.** `runtime/harness_catalogues.py` refreshed a document only
where `path.exists()`, creating one only for a spec declaring
`created_at_startup` — which only Codex did. So the launcher was the sole thing
that could create `~/.fcc/opencode-config.json`. The fetch timed out → the file
was never created → the publisher had nothing to refresh → the next launch
failed identically. The one failure mode that mattered was also the only one the
fallback ("launch without it") could not recover from.

## What changed

**The server owns the files; the launcher reads them.** `mcc-server` now
materialises every MCC-owned harness document at startup and rewrites it on every
catalogue publish. A launcher opens the file it needs and starts the agent with
**no HTTP at all**; it fetches only to create a document that is not there.

The concern the old rule answered was real but misplaced: these documents live
under `~/.fcc`, MCC's own directory, not inside any CLI's configuration folder,
so materialising them leaves nothing behind in a tool's own space.

**Command Code is unchanged and stays merge-on-launch.** Its provider block is
one key inside `~/.commandcode/providers.json`, a file the user wrote. A
`provider.mcc` block must never appear there because a key rotated on a server
they left running, so the fan-out still tests for MCC's own key rather than the
file, and the merge still happens on `mcc-commandcode` only.

**A separate, named budget.** `CATALOGUE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20.0`, its own
constant, a `Settings` field, a `LIMIT_RANGES` bound and a control on **Limits &
Resilience → Deadlines**. The floor is **1 s, not 0**: every other deadline in
this product reads 0 as "no limit", but `urlopen(timeout=0)` fails before it
connects, so a 0 here would mean "never build a missing document" — the deadlock
again, spelled differently.

**Provenance is opt-in.** `?provenance=1` for a caller that wants the per-field
ladder record; off by default for the launchers and the publisher.

**The warning is honest.** It names the file it expected, the request it tried,
the budget it had, the variable that sets it, and the two things a user can do:

```
My Claude Code warning: no OpenCode model list at C:\...\slowhome\.fcc\opencode-config.json, and building one failed: timed out.
  Tried GET http://127.0.0.1:8399/admin/api/catalogue-models with a 3s budget (CATALOGUE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS).
  Start the server with mcc-server, or run mcc-opencode again once the dashboard's Coding agents page shows this agent's catalogue. Launching without an MCC provider.
```

**Dropped the `options.headers.Authorization` override** from the OpenCode
family's document (shared by OpenCode, OpenCode 2 and Kilo, which reuse the same
serialiser). Its comment said `@ai-sdk/anthropic` sends `x-api-key`, "which MCC
does not read" — true when it was written, wrong since 6.27.0, where
`api/dependencies.py::_presented_proxy_token` reads exactly that header. One
credential now, in one place, spelled the way the SDK spells it.

## Measurements

Scratch MCC on `127.0.0.1:8199` with a scratch `HOME`, one custom provider
pointed at a fake gateway on 8299, 292 models seeded from the models.dev cache to
match the reporting install's shape. The live 8082 was read-only throughout;
`~/.fcc` and `~/.config/opencode` were never touched.

### The route

```
no-provenance  t=0.866136s http=200 bytes=2053918
no-provenance  t=0.863243s http=200 bytes=2053918
no-provenance  t=0.802152s http=200 bytes=2053918
provenance=1   t=1.563053s http=200 bytes=3478188
provenance=1   t=1.508029s http=200 bytes=3478188
provenance=1   t=1.537788s http=200 bytes=3478188
```

Provenance costs **~0.70 s and 1.42 MB** on 292 models with a warm index, and
nothing on this route reads it. That is what the launchers stop paying.

### Materialisation at startup

All eleven MCC-owned documents present after one `mcc-server` start, JSON, TOML
and Aider's two-file pair alike; Command Code's `providers.json` correctly still
absent:

```
aider-model-metadata.json  aider-model-settings.yml  cline/  codex-model-catalog.json
crush/  droid-settings.json  gemini-cli-settings.json  kilo-config.json
kimi-code-config.toml  opencode-config.json  opencode2-config.json
qwen-code-settings.json
```

`GET /admin/api/harnesses` reports `exists: true` and an `updated_at` for all
eleven, `exists: false` for `commandcode_cli`.

### The launches

```
----- mcc-opencode models mcc (file ABSENT -> one fetch) -----
rc=0 elapsed=6.50s
--- stdout mcc/ count: 293 ---
My Claude Code: 193 model(s) carry a value OpenCode supplied because no provider published one (...)
-rw-r--r-- 192962 .../live/.fcc/opencode-config.json

----- mcc-opencode models mcc (file PRESENT -> no fetch) -----
rc=0 elapsed=4.70s
--- stdout mcc/ count: 293 ---
--- stderr ---
```

The server's own access log is the proof that "no fetch" means no fetch:

```
"GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
"GET /admin/api/catalogue-models HTTP/1.1" 200 OK     <- the absent-file run
"GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 OK                          <- the present-file run, and nothing else
```

### The chat, and the credential

```
----- opencode run via mcc -----
rc=0 elapsed=10.37s
ok
> build · custom_acme/abacus/gpt-5-nano
```

`POST /v1/messages 200`, **zero 401s in the whole session**. The document carries
`options` = `['apiKey', 'baseURL']` and nothing else, so this is the header
override's replacement proving itself: `@ai-sdk/anthropic` sent `x-api-key` and
MCC accepted it.

### A second, non-OpenCode harness

Gemini CLI, same two runs:

```
file ABSENT   -> one catalogue GET (7 -> 8), gemini-cli-settings.json written, 114287 B, 293 models
file PRESENT  -> zero catalogue GETs (8 -> 8)
mcc-gemini -p "say ok"  ->  ok      (POST /v1beta/models/...:streamGenerateContent 200)
```

### A deliberately slow server

A stand-in on 8399 whose `/health` is instant and whose catalogue route sleeps —
the user's failure, reproduced on purpose, with the file absent and a 3 s budget.
It printed the three-line warning quoted above and launched anyway.

## Browser

Coding agents and Limits & Resilience → Deadlines driven in Chrome against the
scratch server. Every catalogue-owning card now shows its path, "Last written"
and its model count, because the document always exists; Command Code's card
correctly reads *"Never - written on the first mcc-commandcode"*. The new field
renders as **Coding agent catalogue build budget** with *"Accepts 1 to 3600 (1s
minimum; 0 would fail the fetch outright rather than wait forever)"* and
*"default: 20"*. **Zero console messages of any kind.** Screenshots:
`screenshots-oc-fix/`.

## Tests

New:

- `tests/cli/test_opencode_launcher.py`
  - `test_a_launcher_uses_the_document_on_disk_without_fetching`
  - `test_a_corrupt_document_on_disk_falls_back_to_a_fetch`
  - `test_a_missing_document_is_fetched_once_with_the_catalogue_timeout_not_the_preflight_one`
  - `test_the_catalogue_budget_is_the_one_the_dashboard_saved`
  - `test_the_catalogue_fetch_never_imports_the_health_check_budget`
  - `test_a_slow_server_never_yields_a_config_less_launch_silently`
  - `test_every_catalogue_owning_launcher_reads_its_document_first`
- `tests/runtime/test_catalogue_fanout.py`
  - `test_the_fan_out_creates_a_missing_document`
  - `test_every_catalogue_format_is_materialised_at_startup`
  - `test_a_toml_catalogue_is_created_as_toml_when_it_is_missing`
- `tests/api/test_admin_harnesses.py`
  - `test_provenance_is_opt_in_on_the_catalogue_route`
  - `test_opencode_document_authenticates_with_apikey_alone`
- `tests/config/test_settings_to_consumer_contract.py`
  - `test_the_catalogue_fetch_budget_reaches_the_launcher_socket`
  - `test_the_catalogue_fetch_budget_is_clamped_to_a_usable_floor`
- `tests/config/test_admin_limits.py` — `CATALOGUE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` added
  to `SECTION_KEYS["deadlines"]`, which is what makes
  `test_no_resilience_field_is_orphaned` and
  `test_every_manifest_default_matches_the_settings_default` cover it.

`tests/contracts/test_every_setting_has_an_admin_field.py` covers the new field
without an edit, by construction.

Full local run: **8,939 passed, 14 failed, 38 skipped**. All fourteen are the
known pre-existing set — 8 websearch / `test_web_server_tools` reading the real
`~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer — and none is in a file this branch
touches. (The documented baseline is 15; the fifteenth,
`test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`, happened to pass
on this run.) jsdom alone with `-n 0`: **203 passed**. `ruff format --check`
repo-wide, `ruff check` and `ty check` over `src/` and `tests/`: clean, no
suppressions added.

## Docs

- `docs/USAGE.md` — a new **How an agent's model list gets to disk** section: the
  files live under `~/.fcc`, the server writes them at startup and on every
  publish, the launcher reads them, the fetch is cold-start only and its budget
  is named; Command Code and Goose called out as the two that work differently;
  the old deadlock recorded in a note so nobody re-derives it.
- `README.md` — the same rule beside the catalogue section, plus the setting's
  row.
- The dashboard **Guide → Point another CLI here** — the same, where the user is.
- `.env.example` — the variable with the 1.5 s vs 1.8–4.0 s reasoning.

## Residual risks

- **The route is still uncached and still serialises thirteen documents to
  answer for one.** With provenance off it is 0.80–0.87 s for 292 models rather
  than 1.8–4.0 s, and it is now paid at most once per agent per machine, so this
  is a real but much smaller cost. `?harness=<id>` and a generation-keyed cache
  belong to a change about the route, with its own measurements — the second also
  touches the Models page's separate 9–13 s problem.
- **No staleness check on the file.** The launcher uses whatever is on disk and
  never asks whether the server has since resolved different capabilities. That
  is correct in the shape MCC actually runs — the launcher's preflight has
  already proved the server is up, and a running server has rewritten every
  document at startup and on every publish — but a document written by a server
  that has since been stopped, upgraded and not yet restarted will be used as-is.
  Deliberate: adding a conditional GET would put an HTTP round-trip back on every
  launch, which is the thing being removed.
- **Cline's per-launch `--model` is re-applied to the on-disk document** rather
  than to a freshly fetched one. That is one small write on a launch that names a
  model, and none otherwise. Cline is not installed on this machine, so that path
  is covered by unit tests only — **UNVERIFIED live**.
- **Aider, Crush, Droid, Kimi, Kilo and Cline were not launched for real** —
  their binaries are not installed here. Their file-first path is identical code
  and is covered by `test_every_catalogue_owning_launcher_reads_its_document_first`
  plus the fan-out materialisation test, and Gemini CLI and Codex exercise the
  same shape live.
- **The 292-model scratch install is a shaped approximation** of the reporting
  machine, not a copy of it: same model count and a real models.dev index, but
  one custom provider instead of theirs. The 1.8–4.0 s figure in this description
  is from the reporting install, measured with `curl`; the 0.80–0.87 s / 1.51–1.56 s
  pair is from the scratch server and is a before/after of provenance only.
- **`opencode2` and `kilo` share the OpenCode serialiser**, so dropping the
  Authorization header changes their documents too. OpenCode v1's live run proves
  the credential; v2 and Kilo are **UNVERIFIED live** (v2's background service did
  not start under a scratch HOME in the earlier investigation, and Kilo is not
  installed).

commit.message:
fix(harnesses): the server writes every agent's model list, the launcher reads it

`mcc-opencode` printed `My Claude Code warning: could not prepare the OpenCode
config (timed out); launching without an MCC provider` and started with no MCC
models in the picker. On the machine that reported it, it would have done that
forever.

Three defects compounded into a deadlock. The launcher's catalogue fetch reused
`PROXY_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.5` -- a budget sized for `GET /health`,
which answers in milliseconds -- for `GET /admin/api/catalogue-models`, which
serialises all thirteen registered harness documents out of the resolution
ladder and measured 1.8-4.0 s on that install (1.41 MB, reproduced 3/3 through
the launcher's own code path). Most of that was provenance: `capability_payload`
walked the ladder once per field per model for 292 models, computed for the
Models page and read by nobody on this route. And the server's fan-out publisher
refreshed only documents that already existed, so the launcher was the sole
thing that could create `~/.fcc/opencode-config.json` -- which meant the fetch
timing out left the file absent, which left the publisher with nothing to
refresh, which left the next launch failing identically.

The generated document was never the problem: OpenCode 1.18.26 loads it and
lists every MCC model with zero errors.

Inverted the ownership. `mcc-server` now materialises every MCC-owned harness
document at startup and rewrites it on every catalogue publish, so a launcher
opens the file and starts the agent with no HTTP at all; it fetches only to
create a document that is not there. Command Code stays merge-on-launch -- its
provider block is one key inside `~/.commandcode/providers.json`, a file the
user wrote, and a block must never appear there because a key rotated on a
server they left running.

The fetch that remains has its own named budget, `CATALOGUE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
(20 s), a `Settings` field, a `LIMIT_RANGES` bound with a 1 s floor -- 0 would
make `urlopen` fail before connecting, which is the deadlock again -- and a
control on Limits & Resilience -> Deadlines. Provenance on the route is now
opt-in behind `?provenance=1`. And the warning is honest: it names the file it
expected, the request it tried, the budget it had and the two things a user can
do about it, instead of naming the symptom and stopping.

Also dropped the `options.headers.Authorization` override from the OpenCode
family's document. Its comment said `@ai-sdk/anthropic` sends `x-api-key`,
"which MCC does not read" -- true when written, wrong since 6.27.0, where
`api/dependencies.py::_presented_proxy_token` reads it. One credential now, in
one place, spelled the way the SDK spells it.

Verification, against a scratch MCC on 8199 with 292 models and a scratch HOME
(the live 8082 was read-only throughout):

  startup materialised all 11 MCC-owned documents; Command Code's stayed absent
  GET /admin/api/catalogue-models         0.80/0.86/0.87 s, 2,053,918 B
  GET /admin/api/catalogue-models?provenance=1  1.51/1.54/1.56 s, 3,478,188 B
  mcc-opencode models mcc, file absent    6.50 s, 293 models, 1 catalogue GET
  mcc-opencode models mcc, file present   4.70 s, 293 models, 0 catalogue GETs
  mcc-opencode run -m mcc/... "say ok"    "ok", POST /v1/messages 200, zero 401s
  mcc-gemini -p "say ok"                  "ok", 0 catalogue GETs on the second run
  a deliberately slow server, file absent -> the three-line warning, then launch

Not done: the route is still uncached and `?harness=<id>` still does not exist,
so a cold start still serialises thirteen documents to use one. Both belong to
a change about the route, with its own measurements.
